model.architecture: Hybrid gated-delta-net: 18 GatedDeltaNet linear-attention layers + 6 gated full-attention layers (KV budget 4096 on the 6 attention layers); text decoder only, vision tower and MTP heads dropped. The upstream checkpoint is multimodal; this repo ships the text decoder and, separately, a fast_vlm build that adds the checkpoint's own 12-layer 768-dim ViT (no DeepStack)

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on decoder linears + embedding (convs and the delta rule stay float); vision encoder fp16, vision adapter int8; prefer_activation_type fp32 declared in-bundle

recommended.reason: image E2E and vision-on-GPU both grounded; GPU decode 2.7x CPU on M4 Max
iPhone 17 Pro Metal: vision grounded 2/2 at 65.8 tok/s, and the composite text probe scores 6/8 on Metal against 3/8 on CPU - prefer GPU

measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 205-token prompt, 2 cold runs per backend, cooled before each run): cpu decodes 32.63 tok/s against gpu's 34.77 (0.9x), prefill 213.9-353.4 vs 551.1-577.5 tok/s, peak 1780 vs 3772 MB, engine init 17.3 vs 74.4 s. Same-device control taken: decode is a wash (within 10%), so the choice rests on the other numbers. The GPU path (fp32 activations) needs a 74 s engine init and 2.1x the peak memory. This puts the vision-capable file on flagship-class phones; the class-less CPU recommendation on the text-only int8 file stays for every other Android phone

platform_notes: Text + one 512x512 image per turn (fast_vlm contract, 256 soft tokens). Text-only prompts work; this file is a superset of the text build
Six-signature prefill ladder (1024,256,64,16,4,1). It fit iPhone Metal on the first export - no jetsam and no maxNumTokens override, unlike the 2B sibling
GPU runs with fp32 activations (declared in-bundle); iPhone Metal peak ~3.8 GB
Positions are 1-D under fast_vlm, so the checkpoint's M-RoPE collapses to plain RoPE - expect same-content paraphrase rather than token-exact agreement with a full M-RoPE reference
Android/Mali not gated for this build; fp16 vision is known to reboot Mali on models of this shape, so an int8-vision build would be the Android path

known_issues: Composite 8-question probe: Mac 8/8 on both backends, iPhone Metal 6/8, iPhone CPU 3/8. None of the device misses reproduce on Mac with the same file and prompt, so they are device-side rather than the conversion; the mechanism is not identified. Prefer GPU on iPhone.

int8 vision encoder holds 0.9916-0.9951 correlation on real photographs (better than the 2B tower's 0.974-0.984), but this file ships the encoder in fp16 - the int8-encoder variant exists locally and is not published.

measured.source: S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (188522 ops across 12 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

known_issues: GPU on Qualcomm Adreno verified once on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24: full delegation, correct answer) but with a 110 s engine init and a 5.4 GB peak, so CPU stays the Android recommendation

An fp16-activation GPU formulation is unfinished (real-weight fp16 range overflow in one layer-0 head — a property of the checkpoint, not the conversion), hence fp32 activations and the GPU memory cost
On a harder composite probe (8 questions in one 138-token prompt) the int8 quantization measurably costs answers at this 0.8B scale; the per-question sanity gate is word-for-word identical to HF fp32
On low-end Android GPUs decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and does not beat the CPU
